title: No Kings, Just Freedom - Pueblo, CO

location.venue: Sister Cities Plaza & Sister Cities Fountain

description:
Join **Pueblo Indivisible, Center for Health Progress, SEIU Colorado, Colorado WINS, Southern Colorado Labor Council, AFSCME, NAACP** and other community partners for **“No Kings. Just Freedom.”** — a Progressive People’s March through downtown Pueblo to reject fascism, fear, and false kings in all their forms.

- ## Saturday, June 14th
- ## 11am - 1pm
- ## Sister Cities Plaza for Main Rally
_(Progressive March starts Main Street & City Center Drive)_

This event is part of Indivisible’s national No Kings Day of Defiance — a coordinated, nationwide action on Flag Day to push back against authoritarianism, extremism, and Trump’s criminal attempt to reclaim the presidency. Across the country, communities like ours are rising up to say:

### No to fascism. No to fear. No to false kings.

In **Pueblo**, we’re proud to bring our own vision and fire to this movement — one rooted in our values, our history, and our hopes for a just, liberated future.

This is more than a protest — it’s a march that grows as we go.
We begin in four small but mighty groups, each just two blocks apart, each rising up for a core freedom under threat.

As each group marches forward, they’re joined by the next — building strength, sound, and solidarity until we arrive together as one people, united in power, at Sister City Plaza.

Along the way, we lift up four essential truths:

- 🩺 **No Kings: Just Healthcare for All** – Because health is a human right, not a privilege for the powerful

- 🗣️ **No Kings: Just Free Speech** – Because truth-telling, protest, and press must remain free

- ✊ **No Kings: Just Workers’ Rights** – Because the people who build this country deserve justice, not exploitation

- 🌍 **No Kings: Just Earth Over Empire** – Because climate justice can’t wait, and the planet belongs to all of us

By the time we reach the rally, we are no longer four separate groups — we are a movement in motion. **One voice. One fight. One future.**

Join us in marching not just against authoritarianism — but for the **world we know is possible.**



### 🎉 After the March & Rally:
Following our protest, we encourage participants to head over to **Ray Aguilera Park** (formerly Bessemer Park and Minnequa Park) located at:
843 W. Northern Ave, Pueblo, CO 81004
There, you can join the city’s official **Juneteenth Celebration** — a space of joy, culture, and deep-rooted community freedom.

We’ll have art installation projects on site so we can continue creating, connecting, and celebrating the liberation we’re all fighting for.

For bridge protests, where visibility from a distance is crucial, the larger the lettering, the better. Here are some key considerations and general guidelines:
General Visibility Rules:
•	Distance is Key: The primary factor is how far away your audience will be. For highway overpasses, traffic might be moving quickly and at a significant distance.
•	"Rule of Thumb" for Legibility: A common guideline for outdoor signage is that each inch of letter height provides approximately 10 feet of legibility. So, for every 100 feet of viewing distance, you'd want at least 10-inch tall letters.
•	Bridge Specifics: Bridges often mean viewing from a greater distance than a sidewalk. Consider vehicles on the road below, and potentially other onlookers further away.
Practical Recommendations for Bridge Protests:
•	Go Big: Aim for lettering that is at least 12-24 inches tall, and even larger if possible. Some sources suggest using 20x30 or 24x30 inch boards for individual letters to create large, impactful messages.
•	Bold, Simple Fonts: Choose block, sans-serif fonts (like Arial or Helvetica) that are thick and easy to read. Avoid thin, ornate, or script fonts.
•	High Contrast Colors: This is critical!
o	Dark letters on a light background (e.g., black on white, dark blue on yellow) offer the best visibility.
o	Avoid low-contrast combinations like yellow on white or light blue on a pale background.
o	Limit your color palette to two or three colors for maximum impact and clarity.
•	Concise Messaging: Shorter messages with fewer words are easier to read quickly from a distance. Each letter takes up space, so a long message will require smaller letters to fit, reducing visibility.
•	Material and Construction:
o	Sturdy materials: Foam core boards or corrugated plastic are more rigid and durable than regular poster board, especially in windy conditions.
o	Weatherproof: Consider if rain or sun will affect your signs. Paint or vinyl letters are more resilient than marker.
o	Double-sided signs: If possible, make your signs double-sided to maximize visibility from different angles, especially for media coverage.
•	Test Your Signs: Before the protest, hold up your signs and have someone view them from a distance similar to what you expect on the bridge. This will help you determine if the lettering is large enough and if the message is clear.
•	Spacing (Kerning): Ensure there is adequate space between letters and words so they don't blend together from a distance.
By focusing on large, bold, high-contrast lettering and concise messages, you'll maximize the impact and readability of your bridge protest signs.

title: New Member Orientation! (Summer Series)
description:
As a member-led youth movement, MOVE Texas Members are at the heart of our mission to transform democracy in Texas and beyond. **Born out of the student organizing movement in San Antonio in 2013,** MOVE Texas was founded by young people who saw a gap in civic engagement and decided to take action. What started as a small group of student leaders registering their peers to vote has since grown into a statewide movement of young people that trains, mobilizes, and empowers a new generation of progressive community organizers.

## Who are MOVE Texas Members?

MOVE Texas members are the backbone of the organization, reflecting the energy and diversity of young Texans leading the charge for a more just and equitable future for all Texans across race, class, and place.  As a youth movement, MOVE Texas members are under 30, and are either:


- **Students:** The original foundation of MOVE Texas—young leaders organizing on campuses across the state, running voter registration drives, educating their peers, and leading local issue-based campaigns.

- **Community Members:** Young Texans who are inspired by MOVE Texas’ mission and actively work to build power in their neighborhoods, from hosting events to advocating for direct local and statewide policy change.

## MOVE Texas members receive:

- Access to MOVE trainings, programs, and resources,

- Voting power for statewide and local campaigns,

- Exclusive invitations to MOVE statewide events,

- Connection to a network of peers organizing across the state,

- Exclusive members merch.


MOVE Texas membership is open to anyone who believes in the power of young people to lead and shape the future AND our present. **By becoming a member, you’re not just supporting a movement—you are the movement.**

title: Defend the Constitution - Unite for Veterans

location.venue: On the corner of Appleway Ave & US-95 in Coeur d' ALene

description:
We will gather together in a spirit of unity and shared purpose, standing side by side on the sidewalk as a visible expression of our unwavering support for the United States Constitution and the rule of law it upholds. title: We Have No Kings In America!
description:
On Flag Day, June 14, 2025 in Dripping Springs, at 10 am, we shall once again gather under the big oaks at the picnic tables at Veterans Park in Downtown Drippin' to exercise our First Amendment Rights.

In light of the fact that "someone" is having a big, unAmerican and very expensive military parade in D.C. that same day, we are going to celebrate our flag and our freedom in our own way, with signs, banners, FLAGS and our cars, painted up like it's Prom Night.  

Our celebration of Freedom and our Rights as Americans will begin, as it does every Saturday morning, with a march to the intersection of RR 12 and Hwy 290 West, to OCCUPY the four corners with our signs and flags flying, while we wave to our neighbors passing by.  

We will also be handing out pocket-sized copies of the U.S. Constitution, just in case some of our neighbors would like to compare what is going on these days, with what the Founding Fathers had in mind.

We have been greeted most Saturdays by friendly waves, thumbs up and honks, but there are always a few who for some reason think we should not be expressing ourselves.  We wave and smile at them, too!

Then, around noonish, we will once again gather under the oaks to organize ourselves into a caravan of cars and trucks, flying our flags, and adorn our vehicles with white shoe polish in the time-honored tradition of Prom Night, weddings and winning the State Championship.  

We will do a little dance around town, our very own version of a Flag Day Parade, then making our way to one of the local watering holes to hoist a cold one, and get some lunch.  Stay tuned for details.

Street theater, costumes, music and dancing is encouraged, as are American flags, PRIDE flags, signs, banners, songs, chants, and dance. 

We invite you to bring anything that helps you to express how you feel about being an American, and how you are not amused at how the current Administration is abusing their power, and wasting our tax dollars marching tanks and soldiers down Pennsylannia Avenue.

Be sure to dress for the summer weather, bring water, snacks, a sun hat, comfy shoes and your love of Democracy.

See you all on June 14, starting at 10 am at Veterans Park in DownTown Dripping Springs, Texas!

description:
On Monday, June 2, Senate & House Democrats will hold a press conference to discuss catastrophic impacts the “big, beautiful bill” will have on Pennsylvania’s hospitals seniors, babies, and SNAP recipients should it be adopted in its current form. 

On May 22, a budget bill that would strip 15 million Americans of health insurance and 3 million families of healthy food was passed in the US House of Representatives. This legislation will be detrimental to Pennsylvania communities and puts incredible pressure on the PA state budget, due June 30, to bridge the funding gap the federal government has now created. These cuts will be especially harmful to local rural areas, where hospitals, often the largest employers of the areas, are the backbone of local economies.

Senate Democrats will join House Democrats to soundly condemn this disastrous bill and call on Republicans in the PA House and Senate to join in protecting Pennsylvania’s access to food and healthcare.

title: Precinct 909 and Friends June Meeting with Special Guest Speaker
description:
Please join us for our June Precinct 909 meeting with special guest Catherine Jourdan on Tuesday June 10, 2025 at 6:30 PM at Reynolda Manor Branch Library! Several other Precincts have been invited and will be joining us!

title: No Kings Safety Marshal Training
description:
We are expecting a very large turnout for our June 14th No Kings March and Rally! Safety marshals wear yellow vests and are connected to the event leaders via text. You will be assigned a specific location to report to before the march, and as the march passes your location you will join the march and continue to the rally location at O'Donnell Park. We will host an in-person and online safety marshal training on Friday, June 6th at 7:00pm. Marshals are the eyes and ears of our event and our goal is to keep everyone as safe as possible.

Participants who wish to attend on Zoom will receive the link via email before the meeting.

title: No Kings Rally - Spearfish

address_lines: North Main Street & West Jackson Street

description:
No Kings Protest – Spearfish

Saturday, June 14 | 11:00 AM – 12:30 PM
North Main & West Jackson, Spearfish

In America, we don’t put up with would-be kings. NO KINGS is a national day of action and mass mobilization in response to increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption from Trump and his allies. We’ve watched as they’ve cracked down on free speech, detained people for their political views, threatened to deport American citizens, and defied the courts. They’ve done this all while continuing to serve and enrich their billionaire allies.

🚨On Saturday, June 14, we’re taking to the streets nationwide. We’re not gathering to feed his ego. We’re building a movement that leaves him behind.🚨

The flag doesn’t belong to Donald Trump. It belongs to us. We’re not watching history happen. We’re making it.

On June 14th, we’re showing up everywhere he isn’t—to say no thrones, no crowns, no kings. Check out nokings.org for more information.

A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.
